formats.key: createSession(address delegate, uint48 validAfter, uint48 validUntil, uint32 maxCalls, uint16 maxFeeBps, (address token, uint256 limit)[] limits, bytes32 salt)
effects: Creates a session owned by the signer (msg.sender) that lets `delegate` sign calls which allowlisted target contracts run against the signer's funds.
Sets a per-token spend allowance for the session for each token in `limits`; a limit of type(uint256).max is never decremented (unlimited).
Bounds the session by the validAfter/validUntil window (validUntil 0 = no expiry) and maxCalls (0 = unlimited calls).
Lets the relayer take a fee of up to maxFeeBps of the output on each call.
Which contracts the delegate can drive is set by the SessionManager admin (allowedTarget), not by this call.
formats.shown: "Session {delegate}" with the delegate, the validity dates, max calls, the max fee in bps and each token limit rendered through its token.

findings.title: createSession intent does not say the delegate gets power to spend the signer's tokens.
findings.evidence: descriptor intent "Create session", interpolatedIntent "Session {delegate}"; SessionManager.sol header: delegate signs per-call intents consumed by targets, and validateAndConsume decrements tokenAllowance of the owner's session.
findings.fix: Use an interpolatedIntent like "Let {delegate} spend your tokens until {validUntil}".

findings.title: createSession shows validUntil 0 and maxCalls 0 literally, but they mean no expiry and unlimited calls.
findings.evidence: SessionManager.sol SessionConfig: `uint48 validUntil; // 0 = no expiry`, `uint32 maxCalls; // 0 = unlimited`; descriptor formats validUntil as date (0 renders as 1970) and maxCalls as raw.
findings.fix: Add a threshold/message or label ("Valid until (0 = never expires)", "Max calls (0 = unlimited)").

findings.title: createSession token limit can render as a bare integer with no token, because limits.[].token is never shown.
findings.evidence: case 0 screen: Token limit "100000000000000000000" for token 0xf7d85ec4…9c9c; descriptor `limits.[]` visible never, no field for `limits.[].token`.
findings.fix: Add a `limits.[].token` addressName/token field so the asset is visible even when its metadata does not resolve.

findings.title: createSession cannot show which target contracts the delegate may drive; the admin sets them in storage.
findings.evidence: SessionManager.sol validateAndConsume: `if (!allowedTarget[msg.sender]) revert TargetNotAllowed`; allowedTarget is set by setAllowedTarget onlyOwner.
findings.fix: None in the descriptor; it could be named in metadata or the intent text.

effects: Makes the signer, who must be the pending owner, the owner of the SessionManager, with control over which target contracts may consume user sessions.
formats.shown: "Accept ownership" under the generic intent "Manage session manager", with no fields.

findings.title: acceptOwnership uses the generic intent "Manage session manager" shared by all admin functions.
findings.evidence: descriptor acceptOwnership intent "Manage session manager"; interpolatedIntent "Accept ownership".
findings.fix: Set intent to "Accept ownership of session manager".

formats.key: createSessionBySig(address owner_, address delegate, uint48 validAfter, uint48 validUntil, uint32 maxCalls, uint16 maxFeeBps, (address token, uint256 limit)[] limits, bytes32 salt, bytes ownerSignature)
effects: Using owner_'s EIP-712 signature, creates a session for owner_ (not the caller) that lets `delegate` sign calls which allowlisted targets run against owner_'s funds.
Sets per-token session allowances from `limits` (max = unlimited), the validity window (validUntil 0 = no expiry), maxCalls (0 = unlimited) and the max relayer fee.
Moves none of the signer's (relayer's) assets.
formats.shown: "Sig session {delegate}" with the owner, delegate, dates, max calls, max fee in bps and each token limit with its token.

findings.title: createSessionBySig interpolated intent "Sig session {delegate}" is jargon and omits the owner whose funds are delegated.
findings.evidence: descriptor interpolatedIntent "Sig session {delegate}"; case 1 reader unsure "Why the Owner differs from my wallet address, and whose funds the session controls".
findings.fix: Use "Create session for {owner_}: {delegate} may spend listed tokens".

findings.title: createSessionBySig shows validUntil 0 and maxCalls 0 literally, but they mean no expiry and unlimited calls.
findings.evidence: SessionManager.sol SessionConfig comments `0 = no expiry`, `0 = unlimited`; descriptor date and raw formats.
findings.fix: Add a message/threshold or explanatory labels.

findings.title: createSessionBySig token limit has no token field, so an unresolved token shows a bare integer.
findings.evidence: descriptor `limits.[]` visible never, no `limits.[].token` field; same layout as createSession, where case 0 rendered a raw limit.

cases.notes: Mined tx has no token movements. The signer is a relayer, and the session belongs to owner 0x07F9…aA15, which the screen shows. The reader correctly saw four unlimited token limits for a 24h, 100-call session.

formats.key: invalidateNonceBySig(bytes32 sessionId, uint256 nonce, uint256 deadline, address executor, bytes delegateSignature)
effects: Using the delegate's signature, increments the session's nonce, cancelling the pending delegate-signed call that uses this nonce; the session stays active.
The signer must be `executor`; nothing of the signer's moves.
formats.shown: "Invalidate nonce {nonce}" with the session ID as a raw hash, the nonce and the executor.

findings.title: invalidateNonceBySig identifies the session only by a raw bytes32 id; the owner and delegate cannot be shown.
findings.evidence: descriptor field sessionId format raw; sessions[sessionId] holds owner/delegate in storage.

effects: Sets the SessionManager owner to the zero address for good, freezing the target allowlist; the signer loses admin rights.
formats.shown: "Renounce ownership" under the generic intent "Manage session manager".

findings.title: renounceOwnership does not say the step is permanent and freezes the target allowlist.

effects: Marks the signer's session as revoked, so its delegate can no longer have calls validated; only the session owner can call this.
formats.shown: "Revoke {sessionId}" with the session ID as a raw hash.

findings.title: revokeSession shows only a raw session hash; which delegate loses access is in storage.
findings.evidence: descriptor sessionId format raw; case 2 reader unsure "What the session was allowed to do, and who held it".

cases.notes: No token effects. The reader correctly understood that a session is cancelled.

formats.key: revokeSessionBySig(bytes32 sessionId, uint256 deadline, bytes ownerSignature)
effects: Using the owner's signature, marks the session as revoked so its delegate can no longer act; the signer (relayer) moves no assets.
formats.shown: "Revoke sig {sessionId}" with the session ID as a raw hash.

findings.title: revokeSessionBySig interpolated intent "Revoke sig" reads as revoking a signature, not a session.
findings.evidence: descriptor interpolatedIntent "Revoke sig {sessionId}"; code `revoked[sessionId] = true` in _revokeSessionBySig.

effects: Admin only: adds a contract to or removes it from the allowlist of targets that may consume any user's session and spend its token allowances.
formats.shown: "Allow {target}: {allowed}" with the target and a raw true/false.

findings.title: setAllowedTarget shows the bool raw; "Allow X: false" actually disallows the target.
findings.evidence: descriptor interpolatedIntent "Allow {target}: {allowed}", field allowed format raw; case 8 screen "Allow 0xAa48…D23C: true".
findings.fix: Use an enum/label mapping true→"Allow", false→"Remove", and an intent like "Set session target {target}".

effects: Admin only: adds each listed contract to or removes it from the allowlist of targets that may consume user sessions and spend their token allowances.
formats.shown: "Allow targets: {allowed}" with each target address and a raw true/false.

findings.title: setAllowedTargets intent "Allow targets: true" shows a raw bool and reads wrong for false.
findings.evidence: descriptor interpolatedIntent "Allow targets: {allowed}"; case 9 screen "Allow targets: true".
findings.fix: Map the bool to Allow/Remove and say "Allow session targets".

cases.notes: No token effects. The reader correctly saw two addresses added to the allowlist.

effects: Admin only (Ownable2Step): sets newOwner as pending owner. Ownership moves only when newOwner calls acceptOwnership; until then the signer stays owner.
formats.shown: "Transfer to {newOwner}" with the new owner address.

findings.title: transferOwnership says "Transfer to" without naming ownership, and implies an immediate change that is only a nomination.
findings.evidence: descriptor interpolatedIntent "Transfer to {newOwner}"; Ownable2Step.transferOwnership sets `_pendingOwner` only. Case 5 reader: "You likely lose owner control".

cases.notes: No token effects. The reader thought control passes right away; it does so only after acceptance.

formats.key: validateAndConsume(address spendToken, uint256 spendAmount, (bytes32 sessionId, bytes32 dataHash, uint256 nonce, uint256 deadline, address executor, uint256 feeAmount) call, bytes delegateSignature, address executor)
effects: Reverts unless the caller is an allowlisted target contract; an ordinary wallet cannot succeed.
Uses one nonce of the session given in call.sessionId and lowers that session's allowance for spendToken by spendAmount (unless the allowance is unlimited).
Moves no tokens itself; it returns the owner, the delegate and maxFeeBps to the target.
formats.shown: "Validate {spendAmount}" with the spend amount in spendToken; the session, the executor and the fee are hidden.

findings.title: validateAndConsume can only be called by an allowlisted target contract; a wallet signer always reverts.
findings.fix: Consider dropping this format, or note in the intent that it is a contract-only call.

findings.title: validateAndConsume "Validate 25 FT" suggests tokens are spent; only the session's allowance accounting changes, and the session is hidden.
findings.evidence: code `tokenAllowance[call.sessionId][spendToken] = allowance - spendAmount`, no transfer; descriptor call.sessionId and call.feeAmount visible never; case 10 screen "Validate 25 FT".
findings.fix: Use "Consume session allowance of {spendAmount}" and show call.sessionId.
